q: Which laptop component is most commonly replaced using the bottom access panel without disassembling the entire unit?
explanation: Laptops expose RAM and storage under a bottom access panel so they can be upgraded without a full teardown.

q: A laptop will not power on even when plugged in. The AC adapter light is solid. What is the FIRST component to suspect?
explanation: A solid AC adapter light confirms the adapter is functional. The DC jack (where the adapter plugs into the laptop) is the next point of failure: the jack can break loose from the motherboard solder points, interrupting power delivery. Suspect the DC jack before the motherboard itself. Note: a broken

q: What type of drive interface is used by most modern ultrabooks for internal storage?
explanation: Modern ultrabooks use NVMe M.2 SSDs — compact and far faster than SATA.

q: A technician needs to upgrade the wireless card in a laptop. Which interface does the wireless card most commonly use?
explanation: Laptop Wi-Fi cards are usually Mini PCIe or (newer) M.2 modules.

q: Which tool is essential when working inside a laptop to prevent electrostatic discharge?
explanation: An ESD/anti-static wrist strap drains static charge so you don't damage sensitive components.

q: A laptop keyboard stops working after a liquid spill. The FIRST step a technician should take is:
options: Power off and remove the battery
explanation: After a spill, cut power and remove the battery first to prevent a short before doing anything else.

q: What does the acronym SO-DIMM stand for?
options: Small Outline Dual In-line Memory Module
explanation: SO-DIMM stands for Small Outline Dual In-line Memory Module — the compact RAM form factor used in laptops.

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of DDR4 SO-DIMM compared to DDR3?
options: Same pin count, different notch position
Higher pin count and lower voltage
explanation: DDR4 SO-DIMMs have more pins (260 vs DDR3's 204) and run at a lower voltage (1.2 V vs 1.5 V).

q: A laptop hard drive makes a clicking sound on startup. What is the MOST likely cause?
explanation: A clicking laptop drive means failing read/write heads — a mechanical failure, so back up immediately.

q: Which storage form factor is 2.5 inches and commonly used in laptops?
explanation: The 2.5-inch form factor (SATA SSD or HDD) is the common laptop drive size.

q: A technician replaces a laptop thermal paste. What should be done FIRST before applying new paste?
options: Apply new paste directly over old
Run the laptop to warm up the CPU
Clean off old paste with isopropyl alcohol
Remove the fan only, leave the heatsink
explanation: Clean off the old thermal paste with isopropyl alcohol before applying fresh paste for good heat transfer.

q: Which of the following best describes a laptop docking station?
explanation: A docking station expands a laptop's connectivity with extra ports (display, USB, Ethernet, etc.).

q: What is the purpose of a laptop heat pipe?
options: Transfers heat from the CPU to the heatsink and fan
Connects the CPU to the motherboard
explanation: A heat pipe moves heat from the CPU to the heatsink and fan, where it is dissipated.

q: A technician opens a laptop to replace the battery. After reassembly, the touchpad stops working. The MOST likely cause is:
options: Touchpad ribbon cable disconnected during reassembly
explanation: A touchpad that dies right after reassembly usually has its ribbon cable unseated.

q: Which laptop component stores the system firmware and BIOS settings?
options: EEPROM flash chip on the motherboard
explanation: The BIOS/UEFI firmware is stored on an EEPROM/flash chip on the motherboard.

q: A user sees "96% plugged in, not charging." What is the MOST likely explanation?
options: Battery protection circuit preventing overcharge near full capacity
explanation: The Battery Management System (BMS) inside the battery pack intentionally stops charging at approximately 95–100% to prevent cell damage from overcharging. This is normal behavior. Distinguish from a swollen battery (hardware defect requiring immediate replacement) or a BMS fault (battery won't char

q: What display technology offers the best contrast ratio and true blacks by turning off individual pixels?
explanation: OLED turns individual pixels fully off, giving the best contrast ratio and true blacks.

q: A laptop display has a dim image but content is clearly visible. The MOST likely failed component is:
explanation: A dim but readable image points to a failed backlight (inverter/LED driver), not the LCD data path.

q: Which connector type carries both video and power to modern laptop LCD panels internally?
explanation: Internal laptop panels connect via eDP (Embedded DisplayPort), which carries video and power.

q: A laptop screen is cracked but shows an image on an external monitor. What does this confirm?
options: The LCD panel is damaged, not the GPU
explanation: An image on an external monitor while the laptop screen is cracked confirms the LCD panel is at fault, not the GPU.

q: What is the function of a digitizer in a touchscreen laptop?
options: Converts touch input to digital coordinates
explanation: A digitizer converts touch or pen contact into digital X-Y coordinates the OS can use.

q: Which display panel type is known for the fastest response times and is popular for gaming?
explanation: TN panels have the fastest response times, which is why gamers favor them (trading off color and viewing angles).

q: A technician replaces a laptop LCD but the replacement is slightly dimmer. The MOST likely reason is:
options: Wrong backlight voltage or incompatible panel model
explanation: A dimmer replacement panel usually means a mismatched backlight voltage or an incompatible panel model.

q: Which mobile display type uses a separate backlight and cannot achieve true black?
explanation: LCDs rely on a separate backlight, so they cannot switch pixels fully off for true black.

q: A user reports their laptop screen flickers randomly. Testing with an external monitor shows no flicker. The MOST likely component at fault is:
options: Laptop display cable or LCD panel
explanation: Flicker on the laptop screen but not on an external display points to the laptop's display cable or LCD panel.

q: What does "glossy" vs "matte" refer to in laptop screens?
options: Screen coating that affects glare and reflection
explanation: Glossy vs matte describes the screen coating — glossy looks vivid but reflects glare, matte diffuses it.

q: Which technology allows a stylus to be used on a tablet display by detecting electromagnetic signals from the pen?
explanation: An active digitizer (EMR) senses the pen's electromagnetic signal for precise stylus input.

q: A mobile device screen responds to touches in the wrong location. This is MOST likely a:
explanation: Touches registering in the wrong spot indicate a digitizer fault or a touchscreen calibration problem.

q: What is the typical first step when replacing a laptop display assembly?
options: Disconnect power and remove the battery
Detach the display cable from the motherboard
explanation: Always disconnect power and remove the battery first before opening a laptop to replace the display.

q: Which display specification describes the number of pixels per inch?
explanation: PPI (pixels per inch) measures pixel density — a higher PPI looks sharper.

q: A laptop screen shows vertical colored lines but an external display works fine. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: Damaged LCD panel or loose video cable
explanation: Vertical colored lines on the laptop screen but a clean external image point to a damaged LCD panel or loose video cable.

q: A user wants to connect their laptop to a wired network using a USB-C port only. What device do they need?
explanation: A USB-C hub (or dock) with an Ethernet port adds wired networking to a laptop that has only USB-C.

q: Which mobile port standard supports both data transfer and video output up to 40 Gbps?
explanation: Thunderbolt 3/4 carries both data and video at up to 40 Gbps over a USB-C connector.

q: A user connects a smartphone to a laptop via USB and wants to transfer files. The phone shows "Charging only." What setting must be changed on the phone?
options: MTP (Media Transfer Protocol) or file transfer mode
explanation: Set the phone's USB mode to MTP/file-transfer (not 'charging only') to move files.

q: What does USB OTG (On-The-Go) allow a mobile device to do?
options: Act as a USB host to connect peripherals such as drives and keyboards
explanation: USB OTG lets a phone act as a USB host so it can use drives, keyboards, and other peripherals.

q: A laptop only has modern ports (USB-C, HDMI). A user needs to connect a legacy VGA projector. What is needed?
explanation: A legacy VGA projector needs an active HDMI-to-VGA adapter, which converts the digital signal to analog.

q: A user wants to use Bluetooth headphones with their laptop. Bluetooth is turned off and grayed out in settings. The MOST likely cause is:
options: Physical or software wireless disable switch is engaged
Bluetooth is not available on this laptop
explanation: Bluetooth grayed out usually means a hardware or software wireless kill switch is engaged.

q: What is the approximate maximum range for standard Bluetooth Class 2 communication?
explanation: Bluetooth Class 2 (most phones and laptops) has a range of about 10 meters.

q: A user plugs a USB device into a laptop port and gets "USB device not recognized." The FIRST step to troubleshoot is:
options: Try a different USB port on the laptop
explanation: First try a different USB port to rule out one bad port before suspecting the device itself.

q: Which mobile accessory uses NFC for contactless payment?
options: Digital wallet (e.g., Apple Pay, Google Pay)
explanation: Digital wallets like Apple Pay and Google Pay use NFC for contactless tap-to-pay.

q: What connector type is used by most modern Android phones for charging and data?
explanation: Most modern Android phones charge and transfer data over USB-C.

q: A user wants to charge their laptop and connect two 4K monitors using a single cable. Which technology supports this?
explanation: A Thunderbolt 4 dock can drive dual displays and charge the laptop over a single cable.

q: What is the purpose of a port replicator?
options: Provide additional ports to a laptop without a full docking station
explanation: A port replicator adds extra ports to a laptop — a simpler alternative to a full docking station.

q: A mobile device can send files to nearby devices without pairing. What technology is being used?
options: AirDrop or Nearby Share (using Wi-Fi Direct and Bluetooth)
explanation: Sending files to nearby devices without pairing uses AirDrop/Nearby Share (Wi-Fi Direct plus Bluetooth).

q: Which USB specification introduced the reversible connector design?
explanation: USB-C introduced the reversible connector, so there is no wrong-way-up orientation.

q: A laptop does not recognize an SD card. The card works fine in another device. What should the technician check?
options: Card format compatibility and SD card reader driver
explanation: If the SD card works in another device, check the laptop's card-format compatibility and reader driver.

q: What is the primary purpose of enabling developer mode on a mobile device?
options: Access advanced debugging and USB debugging features
explanation: Developer mode exposes advanced debugging features, including USB debugging, on a mobile device.

q: Which protocol is connection-oriented and guarantees delivery of packets?
explanation: TCP is connection-oriented and guarantees ordered, reliable delivery; UDP is connectionless and does not.

q: What port does HTTP use by default?
explanation: HTTP uses TCP port 80 by default.

q: Which protocol uses port 443?
explanation: HTTPS (encrypted web traffic) uses port 443.

q: A technician needs to securely transfer files to a remote server. Which protocol should be used instead of FTP?
explanation: SFTP or FTPS adds encryption, so use them instead of plaintext FTP for secure transfers.

q: Which port does SMTP use for sending email?
explanation: SMTP sends outgoing email on port 25.

q: POP3 uses port ___ to retrieve email from a server.
explanation: POP3 retrieves email from the server on TCP port 110.

q: Which protocol uses ports 137-139 and 445 for Windows file sharing?
explanation: SMB handles Windows file sharing over ports 137-139 and 445.

q: What port does RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) use?
explanation: RDP uses TCP port 3389.

q: What is the primary advantage of a managed switch over an unmanaged switch?
options: Managed switches use wireless instead of wired
Managed switches allow configuration of VLANs, QoS, and port monitoring
explanation: Managed switches let you configure VLANs, QoS, and port monitoring; unmanaged switches cannot be configured.

q: A device that operates at OSI Layer 3 and routes traffic between different networks is a:
explanation: A router works at OSI Layer 3 and routes traffic between different networks using IP addresses.

q: What device connects network segments and forwards traffic based on MAC addresses?
explanation: A switch forwards frames based on MAC addresses, connecting devices within a LAN.

q: A PoE switch provides what key benefit?
options: Wireless connectivity to all connected devices
Power delivery over Ethernet cable to connected devices such as IP cameras
explanation: Power over Ethernet carries both power and data on one cable to devices like IP cameras and access points.

q: What is the purpose of a patch panel in a network rack?
options: Provides centralized termination points for structured cabling
explanation: A patch panel is a central termination point for structured cabling, keeping cable runs organized.

q: What networking device extends the range of a wireless network by receiving and retransmitting the signal?
explanation: A wireless repeater/extender receives the signal and rebroadcasts it to extend coverage.

q: Which device is used to physically connect a computer to a telephone line for DSL access?
explanation: A DSL modem connects the computer to the telephone line for DSL internet.

q: What is the maximum number of devices that can be directly connected to a standard 24-port switch?
explanation: A 24-port switch directly connects 24 devices; more can be added via uplinks or stacking.

q: A NIC (Network Interface Card) operates at which OSI layer?
explanation: A NIC operates at Layer 2 (Data Link), handling MAC addressing and frames.

q: Which Wi-Fi standard operates exclusively on the 5 GHz band and supports speeds up to approximately 3.5 Gbps theoretically?
explanation: Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac) runs on the 5 GHz band with multi-gigabit theoretical speeds.

q: What Wi-Fi standard first introduced MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output) and operates on both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz?
explanation: 802.11n (Wi-Fi 4) introduced MIMO and is the first dual-band standard. Note: MU-MIMO (Multi-User MIMO) was introduced later with 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5).

q: Which wireless security protocol is considered the strongest for WLANs currently?
explanation: WPA3 is currently the strongest Wi-Fi security protocol.

q: What does SSID stand for?
options: Service Set Identifier (the wireless network name)
explanation: SSID stands for Service Set Identifier — the broadcast name of a wireless network.

q: Which 802.11 standard is also known as Wi-Fi 6?
explanation: 802.11ax is branded Wi-Fi 6.

q: What does MIMO stand for in wireless networking?
explanation: MIMO = Multiple Input, Multiple Output — multiple antennas send and receive streams at once to raise throughput.

q: What encryption standard is used by WPA2?
explanation: WPA2 uses AES (CCMP) for encryption.

q: Which wireless standard is designed for short-range, high-bandwidth applications near 60 GHz?
explanation: 802.11ad (WiGig) uses the 60 GHz band for very high bandwidth over short range.

q: A DNS server resolves:
explanation: DNS resolves human-readable hostnames to IP addresses.

q: What service allows users to send and receive email across a network?
options: Mail server using SMTP, IMAP, and POP3
explanation: A mail server sends and receives email using SMTP, IMAP, and POP3.

q: A file server provides what primary function?
options: Centralized storage and access to files over the network
explanation: A file server provides centralized network storage and shared file access.

q: What does a proxy server do?
options: Converts domain names to IP addresses
Acts as an intermediary between clients and the internet, providing caching and filtering
explanation: A proxy sits between clients and the internet, adding caching and content filtering.

q: Which service manages and authenticates users in a Windows domain environment?
explanation: Active Directory (via LDAP) authenticates and manages users in a Windows domain.

q: What is the purpose of a syslog server?
options: Collect and store log messages from network devices
explanation: A syslog server collects and stores log messages from network devices for review.

q: What protocol is used to synchronize clocks on network devices?
explanation: NTP (Network Time Protocol) synchronizes clocks across network devices.

q: A TFTP server is commonly used for:
options: Network device firmware updates and booting diskless workstations
explanation: TFTP is simple and unauthenticated — used for device firmware pushes and booting diskless workstations.

q: What is the purpose of a UTM (Unified Threat Management) appliance?
options: Combine firewall, IDS/IPS, antivirus, and other security functions in one device
Manage multiple switches from one interface
explanation: A UTM appliance bundles firewall, IDS/IPS, antivirus, and more into a single device.

q: What IP address range do most home routers assign by default via DHCP?
explanation: Most home routers hand out addresses on 192.168.1.0/24 by default.

q: A home user wants to prevent specific devices from connecting to their Wi-Fi. What feature accomplishes this?
explanation: MAC address filtering allows or denies specific devices by their hardware (MAC) address.

q: What does disabling SSID broadcast accomplish on a home network?
options: Hides the network name from casual scanning (security through obscurity)
explanation: Disabling SSID broadcast hides the network name from casual scans — security through obscurity, not real protection.

q: A technician is setting up a SOHO network using 192.168.1.0. What subnet mask should be used for a standard home network?
explanation: A standard home network uses 255.255.255.0 (/24), which gives 254 usable host addresses.

q: Which cable type is used for standard Ethernet in a SOHO environment?
explanation: SOHO Ethernet uses Cat5e or Cat6 twisted-pair cabling.

q: A new device can connect to Wi-Fi but cannot reach the internet. All other devices work fine. What should be checked FIRST?
options: The device IP configuration — correct IP, subnet mask, gateway, and DNS
explanation: A device on Wi-Fi but with no internet usually has a bad IP configuration — check IP, subnet mask, gateway, and DNS first.

q: What does NAT accomplish in a SOHO router?
options: Translates private internal IPs to a single public IP for internet access
explanation: NAT translates many private internal IP addresses to one public IP for internet access.

q: Which SOHO router setting restricts internet access for children during certain hours?
options: Parental controls or content filtering with time restrictions
explanation: Parental/content-filtering controls with time limits restrict a child's access during set hours.

q: What is the purpose of QoS settings on a SOHO router?
options: Prioritize certain types of traffic such as video calls or gaming over other traffic
explanation: QoS prioritizes latency-sensitive traffic like video calls and gaming over bulk traffic.

q: What is a VLAN?
options: A logically separated network within a physical switch infrastructure
explanation: A VLAN logically separates one physical switch into independent networks.

q: What is the default gateway used for on a network?
options: Routes traffic from the local network to external networks
explanation: The default gateway routes traffic from the local network out to other (external) networks.

q: A device has IP 192.168.1.50 with subnet mask 255.255.255.0. What is the network address?
explanation: With a /24 mask the host portion zeroes out, so the network address is 192.168.1.0.

q: What does a subnet mask of /24 (255.255.255.0) indicate?
options: 24 bits for network, 8 bits for hosts, allowing 254 usable host addresses
explanation: A /24 uses 24 network bits and 8 host bits, giving 254 usable host addresses.

q: Which DNS record type maps a hostname to an IPv4 address?
explanation: An A record maps a hostname to an IPv4 address (AAAA is used for IPv6).

q: What is DNS cache poisoning?
options: Corrupting DNS cache entries to redirect users to malicious sites
explanation: DNS cache poisoning corrupts cached entries to redirect users to malicious sites.

q: Which internet connection type uses telephone infrastructure and requires a filter to separate voice and data signals?
explanation: DSL rides telephone wiring and needs filters to separate voice from data signals.

q: What type of network spans a single building or campus?
explanation: A LAN covers a single building or campus.

q: Internet access using cell towers is called:
explanation: Internet access over cell towers is cellular (4G/5G).

q: What is the main advantage of cable internet over DSL?
options: More widely available in rural areas than DSL
Higher speeds using shared coaxial cable infrastructure
explanation: Cable internet typically delivers higher speeds than DSL. Cable runs over coaxial TV infrastructure (shared); DSL runs over telephone lines (dedicated per user). DSL is generally more widely available in rural areas because telephone infrastructure is more ubiquitous than cable TV infrastructure.

q: A WAN connects:
options: Multiple LANs across large geographic distances
Wireless devices in a personal area
explanation: A WAN links multiple LANs across large geographic distances.

q: Which technology uses power lines to transmit network data in homes?
explanation: Powerline Communication (HomePlug) carries network data over a home's electrical wiring.

q: What type of network covers a city or large campus — larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN?
explanation: A MAN spans a city or large campus — bigger than a LAN, smaller than a WAN.

q: Which internet connection type is shared among neighborhood users, meaning speeds can decrease during peak hours?
explanation: Cable internet is shared among neighborhood users, so speeds can drop during peak hours.

q: What does "last mile" refer to in telecommunications?
explanation: Satellite internet uses dish antennas pointed at geostationary satellites (~22,000 miles up) and is the primary broadband option in rural areas lacking cable/fiber. High latency (500–800ms round-trip) is a key characteristic due to signal travel distance.

q: A technician needs to attach an RJ-45 connector to the end of a Cat6 cable. Which tool is required?
explanation: A crimper (RJ-45 crimping tool) is used to physically attach an RJ-45 connector to the cable end, locking the conductors in place. It is used when making patch cables or field-terminating cable runs with plugs.

q: A technician is terminating Cat6 cable into a keystone jack in a wall plate. Which tool is used to seat each conductor into the jack?
explanation: A punchdown tool (impact tool) pushes individual conductors into the IDC (insulation displacement contact) slots of a keystone jack or patch panel (110-block standard). The blade cuts excess wire flush during the punch.

q: After terminating a patch cable, a technician wants to verify that all eight conductors are connected in the correct order and there are no open pairs. Which tool performs this test?
explanation: A cable tester (continuity tester) verifies that each pin on one end maps correctly to the matching pin on the other end. It detects opens (broken conductors), shorts (conductors touching), reversed pairs, and miswires. It does not measure signal quality or bandwidth.

q: A technician cannot locate which port in the patch panel corresponds to the wall jack in room 204. Which tool pair is used to identify the cable?
explanation: A toner probe has two parts: a tone generator attached to one end of the cable injects an audio signal, and the inductive amplifier (probe) detects the signal by proximity — no electrical contact required. This allows tracing cables through walls, ceilings, and patch panels without cutting into anyt

q: A technician suspects a NIC or switch port is faulty but the network cable and switch appear functional. Which tool tests the port in isolation?
explanation: A loopback plug connects the transmit (TX) pair to the receive (RX) pair on the same port. When the NIC or switch port sends a signal, it receives its own signal back. Diagnostic software confirms whether the port hardware is functioning. This test isolates the port from all external cable and netwo

q: A user reports intermittent Wi-Fi drops. The technician suspects channel interference from neighboring networks. Which tool identifies overlapping channels and signal strength?
explanation: A Wi-Fi analyzer (software or dedicated hardware) displays all visible SSIDs, their broadcast channels, signal strength (dBm), and security type. It identifies channel overlap — a common cause of interference on the 2.4 GHz band where only channels 1, 6, and 11 are non-overlapping.

q: A network administrator needs to capture all traffic passing between a firewall and a core switch without disrupting active connections. Which device accomplishes this passively?
explanation: A network tap (test access point) is an inline passive device that copies all traffic to a monitoring port without affecting the live data flow. Unlike a SPAN port on a switch, a tap cannot drop packets due to oversubscription and does not require switch configuration.

q: Which networking tool is specifically designed to remove the outer jacket of a UTP cable without cutting through the inner conductor insulation?
explanation: A cable stripper (jacket stripper) uses an adjustable blade depth that scores and removes only the outer PVC jacket. Cutting too deep damages the insulation on individual conductors, which can cause intermittent faults. A standard wire stripper for solid wire can cut too deep on twisted pair — use t

q: Which tool would a technician use to verify that a newly installed structured cabling run meets Cat6 performance specifications (attenuation, NEXT, return loss)?
explanation: A cable certifier (e.g., Fluke DSX series) performs full electrical characterization: insertion loss, near-end crosstalk (NEXT), return loss, and propagation delay. It certifies compliance with TIA/EIA standards. A basic continuity tester only checks wiring order — it cannot certify performance spec

q: A technician needs to identify which wall port connects to a specific patch panel port in a wiring closet without labeled cables. Which tool should they use?
explanation: A toner probe sends a tone signal down the cable; the inductive amplifier probe detects it at the other end, allowing the technician to identify cable runs. A cable certifier tests electrical performance specifications, not cable tracing.

q: Which cable type uses light pulses and is immune to electromagnetic interference?
explanation: Fiber carries light pulses, so it is immune to electromagnetic interference and spans long distances.

q: What connector is used on standard Cat5e and Cat6 Ethernet cable?
explanation: Cat5e and Cat6 Ethernet cable terminates in an RJ-45 connector.

q: Which cable type is used for cable television and has a center conductor surrounded by shielding?
explanation: Coaxial cable (a center conductor surrounded by shielding) is used for cable TV and cable internet.

q: Which fiber optic connector is small, uses a push-pull locking mechanism, and is commonly found in data center patch panels?
explanation: The LC fiber connector is small with a push-pull latch, common in data-center patch panels.

q: What cable category is rated for 10 Gbps up to 55 meters?
explanation: Cat6 supports 10 Gbps up to about 55 meters (Cat6a extends 10G to 100 m).

q: Which display cable carries both audio and video signals in a single cable?
explanation: HDMI carries both audio and video over a single cable.

q: A technician needs to run cable through a plenum space (HVAC airspace above a drop ceiling). Which cable type is required?
explanation: Plenum-rated cable (CMP) has a fire-resistant jacket required in HVAC plenum airspace.

q: What is the maximum data transfer speed of USB 2.0?
explanation: USB 2.0 (Hi-Speed) tops out at 480 Mbps.

q: Which connector is used for traditional telephone (landline) wall jacks and resembles RJ-45 but is smaller?
explanation: Plenum-rated cable uses a fire-retardant low-smoke jacket required by building codes when cables run through HVAC plenum spaces. PVC jackets release toxic smoke when burned, which would be distributed through the air-handling system. Look for CMP (Communications Multipurpose Plenum) rating.

q: Which USB connector type uses a reversible, oval-shaped plug and is the standard connector for USB 3.1 Gen 2 and Thunderbolt 3/4 devices?
explanation: USB-C is reversible and supports USB 3.1/3.2, Thunderbolt 3/4, and USB4 depending on the device.

q: A technician identifies a 15-pin D-sub connector arranged in three rows of five pins on the back of an older monitor. What interface does this connector belong to?
explanation: VGA uses the HD-15 (D-sub 15) connector with three rows of five pins.

q: What fiber optic connector uses a push-pull square housing and is common in enterprise network equipment and ISP infrastructure?
explanation: SC (Subscriber Connector) has a square push-pull housing. LC is smaller with a latch; ST uses a bayonet twist-lock.

q: A technician sees a port on a workstation with a lightning bolt icon next to a USB-C shaped port. What interface does this indicate?
explanation: The lightning bolt icon identifies a Thunderbolt port; Thunderbolt 3 and 4 use the USB-C physical connector.

q: Which connector type is used by eSATA to connect external storage devices, and how does it differ from an internal SATA connector?
options: eSATA uses a modified 7-pin shielded connector rated for repeated hot-plugging; internal SATA uses an unshielded version of the same pin configuration
eSATA and internal SATA use identical connectors
eSATA uses RJ-45; internal SATA uses a 7-pin L-shaped connector
eSATA uses USB-C; internal SATA uses a proprietary connector
explanation: eSATA uses a similar 7-pin configuration but with a shielded connector designed for external use and repeated connections.

q: A laptop has a Mini DisplayPort. What adapter is needed to connect it to a standard HDMI monitor?
options: No adapter needed — they are the same connector
Mini DisplayPort to HDMI adapter or cable
explanation: Mini DisplayPort and HDMI are different connectors; a passive or active adapter is required.

q: Which connector type is used by the PS/2 interface for keyboards and mice, and what feature distinguishes the keyboard port from the mouse port on a system with both?
options: 6-pin DIN connectors; they are color-coded (purple for keyboard, green for mouse)
RJ-11; distinguished by port labeling only
explanation: PS/2 uses a 6-pin Mini-DIN connector; the keyboard port is purple and the mouse port is green by convention.

q: Which fiber optic connector is small form-factor, uses a latch mechanism, and is the standard choice for SFP/SFP+ transceivers in enterprise switches?
explanation: LC connectors are approximately half the size of SC connectors, use a push-pull latch, and are the standard for SFP and SFP+ transceivers in high-density enterprise switch deployments.

q: A monitor has a white rectangular connector with 24 pins in three rows plus one additional pin. What connector type and signal does this represent?
explanation: DVI-D dual-link uses 24 data pins plus a ground blade. DVI-I adds analog pins for analog signal support. The white rectangular housing is the DVI standard; pin count distinguishes single-link vs dual-link and -D vs -I.

q: A legacy point-of-sale (POS) system uses a 9-pin D-shaped (DE-9) connector for its receipt printer. What interface standard does this connector implement?
explanation: The DE-9 (9-pin D-sub) connector is the standard physical interface for RS-232 serial communications, used in legacy POS terminals, barcode scanners, and serial printers. PS/2 uses a 6-pin Mini-DIN; VGA uses a 15-pin HD-15 D-sub.

q: A technician installs RAM in a dual-channel configuration. What is required for dual-channel to activate?
options: Any two sticks of the same brand
Matched pairs installed in the correct slots, typically alternating slots as per motherboard manual
One stick in each bank regardless of slot
explanation: Dual-channel needs a matched pair of modules installed in the correct (usually alternating) slots per the motherboard manual.

q: What type of RAM includes error-correcting code and is primarily used in servers?
explanation: ECC RAM detects and corrects memory errors and is used primarily in servers.

q: A computer produces beep codes after new RAM is installed. The MOST likely cause is:
options: RAM not fully seated or incompatible with the motherboard
explanation: Beep codes right after a RAM install usually mean the module is not fully seated or is incompatible.

q: What does the specification "DDR4-3200" indicate?
options: DDR4 type RAM with a 3200 MT/s transfer rate
explanation: 'DDR4-3200' means DDR4 memory with a 3200 MT/s transfer rate.

q: Which Windows feature uses hard disk space as an overflow area when physical RAM is full?
explanation: Virtual memory uses the page file (pagefile.sys) on disk as overflow when physical RAM fills up.

q: What is the standard RAM form factor used in desktop computers?
explanation: Desktops use full-size DIMMs (288-pin for DDR4).

q: What specification indicates the CAS latency of a RAM module?
options: CL16 or similar notation such as 16-18-18-38
explanation: CAS latency is written as CL16 (or timings like 16-18-18-38); lower is faster.

q: What should a technician do before installing or removing RAM?
options: Back up the hard drive first
Power off the system and discharge static using an ESD strap or by touching the chassis
explanation: Before handling RAM, power off and discharge static with an ESD strap or by touching the chassis.

q: A technician installs 3200 MHz DDR4 RAM but the BIOS reports it running at 2133 MHz. What must be enabled in BIOS/UEFI to achieve the rated speed?
explanation: High-speed DDR4 kits store overclock profiles in the SPD chip using XMP (Intel) or DOCP (AMD). Without enabling XMP/DOCP in BIOS, the system defaults to the JEDEC standard speed (typically 2133 or 2400 MHz) rather than the rated kit speed.

q: Which storage technology has no moving parts and stores data on flash memory chips?
explanation: An SSD has no moving parts and stores data on flash memory chips.

q: What RAID level provides disk mirroring with data redundancy but no striping?
explanation: RAID 1 mirrors data across drives for redundancy, with no striping.

q: Which RAID level provides striping with parity and requires a minimum of 3 drives?
explanation: RAID 5 stripes data with distributed parity and needs at least 3 drives.

q: A user wants maximum storage capacity across two drives with no redundancy. Which RAID level should be used?
explanation: RAID 0 stripes data across both drives for maximum capacity and speed but provides no redundancy.

q: Which storage device uses magnetic platters and a read/write head?
explanation: A hard drive (HDD) uses spinning magnetic platters and a read/write head.

q: What RPM speed is typical for a standard performance desktop hard drive?
explanation: 7200 RPM is typical for a performance desktop hard drive.

q: An SSD is significantly faster than an HDD primarily because:
options: It runs at a higher voltage
It has no moving parts and uses flash memory for near-instant random access
It uses a different BIOS mode
explanation: SSDs are faster mainly because they have no moving parts and use flash for near-instant random access.

q: Which of the following is NOT a standard RAID level?
explanation: RAID 7 is not a standard implementation.

q: Which storage interface provides the highest sequential performance for an M.2 SSD by communicating directly over PCIe lanes, bypassing the SATA controller?
explanation: NVMe (Non-Volatile Memory Express) communicates directly over PCIe lanes, delivering sequential read speeds of 3,000–7,000+ MB/s versus SATA III's 550 MB/s limit. NVMe and SATA M.2 drives share the same M.2 physical slot but require different controller support.

q: What is the most common desktop motherboard form factor?
explanation: ATX is the most common desktop motherboard form factor.

q: What is the purpose of thermal paste when installing a CPU cooler?
options: Adhesive to hold the cooler in place
Fills microscopic air gaps to improve heat transfer between CPU and cooler
Prevents corrosion on the CPU die
explanation: Thermal paste fills microscopic air gaps between the CPU and cooler to improve heat transfer.

q: Which PCIe slot is used for modern graphics cards?
explanation: Graphics cards use the PCIe x16 slot.

q: What does the chipset on a motherboard control?
options: Communication between the CPU, RAM, storage, and I/O devices
explanation: The chipset manages communication between the CPU, RAM, storage, and I/O devices.

q: A technician installs a new GPU and the system boots to a black screen. The FIRST thing to check is:
options: Ensure the GPU is fully seated in the PCIe x16 slot and all power connectors are attached
explanation: A black screen after installing a GPU — first confirm it is fully seated in the x16 slot with all power connectors attached.

q: What is the purpose of the CMOS battery on a motherboard?
options: Provides backup power for RAM contents
Maintains BIOS/UEFI settings and the real-time clock when the system is powered off
explanation: The CMOS battery maintains BIOS/UEFI settings and the real-time clock while the system is powered off.

q: Which specification describes how fast data moves between the CPU and RAM?
options: Memory bus speed or FSB (Front Side Bus)
explanation: Memory bus speed (front-side bus) describes how fast data moves between the CPU and RAM.

q: What motherboard component manages USB ports, SATA, audio, and other I/O functions?
explanation: The southbridge/PCH handles USB, SATA, audio, and other I/O functions.

q: A POST beep pattern of one long beep followed by two short beeps typically indicates a problem with:
explanation: On AMI BIOS systems, one long beep + two short beeps indicates a video/display subsystem failure. Beep codes are vendor-specific: AMI, Award, and Phoenix each use different patterns for the same errors. Always identify the BIOS vendor before interpreting codes. On Award BIOS, one long + two short al

q: A PCIe x1 network card needs to be installed but the motherboard's only available slots are PCIe x16. Can the x1 card be placed in the x16 slot?
options: No — PCIe x1 cards cannot physically fit in an x16 slot
Yes — a smaller PCIe card fits in any larger slot and operates at x1 bandwidth
Yes — but only if the BIOS is updated first to support cross-slot installation
No — the card would operate at x16 speed and cause electrical damage
explanation: PCIe is backward compatible. A PCIe x1 card physically fits in any larger slot (x4, x8, x16) and operates at x1 bandwidth. The slot width sets the maximum link width; the protocol negotiates the actual width automatically.

q: What PSU form factor is used in standard ATX desktop cases?
explanation: Standard ATX desktop cases use the ATX PSU form factor.

q: A desktop randomly shuts off under heavy load. The MOST likely hardware cause is:
explanation: Random shutdowns under heavy load most often come from an insufficient or failing power supply.

q: What does the 80 Plus certification on a PSU indicate?
options: At least 80% energy efficiency under standard load conditions
explanation: 80 Plus certifies a PSU is at least 80% efficient under standard load conditions.

q: Which PSU connector provides primary power to the motherboard in modern ATX systems?
explanation: The 24-pin ATX main connector supplies primary power to the motherboard.

q: What connector provides supplemental power to high-end graphics cards?
explanation: A 6- or 8-pin PCIe power connector feeds supplemental power to high-end graphics cards.

q: A technician is building a workstation with a high-end GPU and multiple drives. What PSU consideration is most important?
options: Adequate wattage with approximately 20-30% headroom above calculated load
explanation: Pick a PSU with enough wattage plus about 20-30% headroom above the calculated load.

q: Which 80 Plus PSU rating is the first tier certified to reach 90% efficiency at 50% load?
explanation: 80 Plus Platinum is certified at 90/92/89% efficiency at 20/50/100% load. 80 Plus Gold reaches 87/90/87%. The key distinction: Platinum hits 90% at the lower 20% load threshold; Gold only reaches 90% at exactly 50% load. Platinum is the answer for "consistently 90%+."

q: What is the purpose of the 4-pin or 8-pin CPU power connector (EPS12V)?
options: Delivers dedicated 12V power to the CPU voltage regulator modules on the motherboard
explanation: The 4/8-pin EPS12V connector delivers dedicated 12V power to the CPU's voltage regulator modules.

q: Before replacing a PSU, what safety step is essential?
options: Unplug the AC power cord and press the power button to discharge capacitors
Back up all data on the drives
explanation: Before replacing a PSU, unplug the AC cord and press the power button to discharge the capacitors.

q: What does "single-rail" vs "multi-rail" describe on a PSU?
options: How the 12V output power is distributed — single rail has one large 12V output vs. multiple smaller rails
explanation: Single- vs multi-rail describes whether the 12V output is one large rail or several smaller ones.

q: What type of printer uses a laser to create an electrostatic image on a drum and then applies toner?
explanation: A laser printer uses a laser to draw an electrostatic image on a drum, then applies toner to it.

q: Which laser printer component transfers the toner image from the drum to the paper?
explanation: The transfer roller/belt moves the toner image from the drum onto the paper.

q: Which step in the laser printing process "writes" the image onto the photosensitive drum using a laser beam?
explanation: The exposing (writing) step uses the laser to draw the image on the photosensitive drum.

q: A laser printer consistently prints a vertical black line down every page. The MOST likely cause is:
options: Scratch or damage on the drum surface
explanation: A scratch or gouge on the photosensitive drum holds toner in that spot every rotation, producing a consistent vertical black line. Distinguish from: a contaminated primary corona wire (also causes a black line — clean the wire first, cheaper fix), or a defective cleaning blade (causes smearing/strea

q: What protocol allows Windows to automatically discover and install a network printer?
options: WSD (Web Services for Devices) or Bonjour
explanation: WSD (or Bonjour) lets Windows automatically discover and install network printers.

q: Which printer type is the BEST choice for printing multipart carbon copy forms?
explanation: Impact (dot matrix) printers physically strike the paper, so they can print multipart carbon forms.

q: What is the purpose of a DHCP reservation for a network printer?
options: Ensures the printer always receives the same IP address for consistent network access
Provides wireless encryption for print jobs
explanation: A DHCP reservation keeps the printer on the same IP address so clients always find it.

q: A network printer shows "offline" in Windows despite being powered on. The FIRST thing to check is:
options: Verify the printer IP address has not changed and the correct port is configured
explanation: A printer 'offline' but powered on — first verify its IP has not changed and the correct port is configured.

q: What allows printing from any device to a compatible printer over the internet without local drivers?
options: Cloud printing services such as Google Cloud Print or vendor equivalents
explanation: Cloud printing services let any device print to a compatible printer over the internet without local drivers.

q: A print job is stuck in the queue and the printer will not print any subsequent jobs. What Windows service should the technician restart to clear the stuck print queue?
explanation: The Print Spooler service manages print jobs queued to print devices. Stopping the spooler, deleting files in C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS, and restarting the service clears a stuck print queue without rebooting the system.

q: Which laser printer consumable is replaced most frequently?
explanation: The toner cartridge is the most frequently replaced laser-printer consumable.

q: What is the correct sequence of the laser printing process?
options: Clean, Charge, Expose, Develop, Transfer, Fuse
Develop, Charge, Expose, Transfer, Clean, Fuse
Expose, Charge, Transfer, Develop, Fuse, Clean
Charge, Expose, Develop, Transfer, Fuse, Clean
explanation: The laser printing process is Charge, Expose, Develop, Transfer, Fuse, Clean.

q: A laser printer produces faded output even after installing a new toner cartridge. The MOST likely cause is:
options: Toner not properly distributed in the cartridge or wrong cartridge model installed
explanation: Triage in order: (1) Confirm the protective sealing/shipping tape was fully removed from the new cartridge — this is the most common cause of faded output after installation. (2) Shake the cartridge gently side to side to redistribute toner. (3) Verify the cartridge part number matches the printer m

q: What type of printer uses a ribbon and impact pins to strike paper, producing characters?
explanation: Impact (dot matrix) printers use a ribbon and pins that strike the paper to form characters.

q: What maintenance tasks should be performed after replacing inkjet ink cartridges?
options: Calibrate the printer and run a printhead cleaning cycle
explanation: After installing new inkjet cartridges, calibrate the printer and run a printhead cleaning cycle.

q: A thermal receipt printer produces completely blank receipts. The MOST likely cause is:
options: Paper loaded backward with the non-coated side facing the printhead
explanation: Blank thermal receipts usually mean the paper is loaded backward, with the coated (heat-sensitive) side facing away from the head.

q: What protective equipment should be worn when replacing laser printer toner?
options: Latex or nitrile gloves and a dust mask
explanation: Wear nitrile or latex gloves and a dust mask when handling laser toner.

q: How should used toner cartridges be disposed of properly?
options: Through manufacturer recycling programs or designated electronics recycling centers
explanation: Dispose of used toner through manufacturer recycling or designated e-waste centers, not the regular trash.

q: A laser printer produces pages where the toner smears or wipes off when touched. Which component requires replacement?
explanation: The fuser assembly applies heat and pressure to permanently bond toner to paper. If toner smears or rubs off after printing, the fuser is not reaching proper temperature or the pressure rollers are worn, indicating it needs replacement.

q: After an inkjet printer has been unused for several weeks, print quality shows streaks and missing colors. What is the FIRST action a technician should take?
options: Disassemble the printer and manually clean with water
Run the printer's built-in printhead cleaning utility
explanation: Inkjet printheads can clog from dried ink during disuse. Most inkjet printers include a maintenance utility (accessible from printer software or control panel) that purges and primes the nozzles. This should be tried before replacing cartridges.

q: A user connects a USB keyboard and it is not recognized. After trying another USB port with no improvement, what is the NEXT step?
options: Check Device Manager for driver issues or unrecognized devices
explanation: If a different USB port does not help, check Device Manager for driver issues or an unrecognized device.

q: Which display setting controls how many pixels are displayed horizontally and vertically?
explanation: Resolution sets how many pixels are displayed horizontally and vertically.

q: A user reports their second monitor shows a duplicate image instead of extended desktop. What setting needs to change?
options: Display mode in Windows display settings — change from Duplicate to Extend
explanation: A duplicated second monitor is fixed by switching the display mode from Duplicate to Extend.

q: What is the standard refresh rate for most consumer monitors?
explanation: Most consumer monitors run at a standard 60 Hz refresh rate.

q: What type of scanner captures documents by passing a light source over the document and detecting reflected light?
explanation: A flatbed scanner passes a light source over the document and reads the reflected light.

q: Which device converts physical drawings or documents into digital format?
explanation: A scanner converts physical documents or drawings into digital files.

q: What is the primary purpose of a barcode reader in a retail environment?
options: Scan and decode barcode data for point-of-sale systems
explanation: A barcode reader scans and decodes barcode data for point-of-sale systems.

q: Which cloud service model provides virtualized computing resources such as VMs over the internet?
explanation: IaaS provides virtualized compute (VMs, storage, networking) delivered over the internet.

q: What cloud deployment model is used exclusively by a single organization?
explanation: A private cloud is used exclusively by a single organization.

q: A company uses both on-premises infrastructure and a public cloud provider simultaneously. This is called a:
explanation: Using on-premises infrastructure together with a public cloud is a hybrid cloud.

q: What is "elasticity" in cloud computing?
options: Physical flexibility of cloud server hardware
Cost reduction over time through usage
Ability to automatically scale resources up or down based on demand
explanation: Elasticity is automatically scaling resources up or down based on current demand.

q: Which cloud characteristic allows users to provision services without human interaction from the provider?
explanation: On-demand self-service lets users provision resources themselves, without provider interaction.

q: What is the MAIN advantage of cloud-based file storage such as OneDrive or Google Drive for end users?
options: Access files from any device with automatic backup and synchronization
Faster local file access compared to local drives
Better security than all local storage options
explanation: Cloud file storage lets you reach files from any device, with automatic backup and synchronization.

q: Which cloud service model provides a development platform including OS, middleware, and runtime environment?
explanation: PaaS provides a ready development platform — OS, middleware, and runtime — to build applications on.

q: What does "multi-tenancy" mean in cloud computing?
options: Multiple data centers in different regions
Multiple customers sharing the same physical infrastructure
Multiple administrators managing one cloud account
explanation: Multi-tenancy means multiple customers share the same physical infrastructure, kept logically separate.

q: Which cloud characteristic ensures services are accessible from any device and location over the network?
explanation: Broad network access means the service is reachable from any device and location over the network.

q: What is the MAIN concern with storing sensitive data in a public cloud environment?
options: Data privacy, compliance requirements, and shared infrastructure security risks
Slower access speeds compared to local storage
Higher cost than all on-premises options
explanation: The main concern is data privacy, compliance requirements, and shared-infrastructure security risk.

q: Which of the following is an example of SaaS?
explanation: Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace are SaaS — ready-to-use applications delivered over the web.

q: What is a CDN (Content Delivery Network) used for?
options: Distributing content geographically closer to users to reduce latency
explanation: A CDN caches content on servers geographically closer to users to reduce latency.

q: What does "cloud bursting" refer to?
options: Migrating all workloads to the cloud permanently
Automatically offloading excess workloads to the public cloud when on-premises capacity is exceeded
explanation: Cloud bursting offloads overflow workloads to the public cloud when on-premises capacity is exceeded.

q: Which cloud characteristic tracks resource usage for billing and audit purposes?
explanation: Measured service meters resource usage for billing and auditing.

q: A company migrates its email server to Microsoft 365. Which cloud model does this represent?
explanation: Moving email to Microsoft 365 is consuming a finished application, which is SaaS.

q: What is the purpose of a cloud access security broker (CASB)?
options: Manage cloud billing and cost allocation
Enforce security policies between cloud users and cloud service providers
explanation: A CASB enforces security policies between cloud users and cloud service providers.

q: Which term describes the process of moving applications and data from on-premises to a cloud environment?
explanation: Cloud migration is the process of moving applications and data from on-premises to the cloud.

q: What is DaaS (Desktop as a Service)?
options: Virtual desktop environments hosted in the cloud and accessed remotely by users
Data backup delivered as a service
explanation: DaaS (Desktop as a Service) delivers cloud-hosted virtual desktops that users access remotely.

q: A small business wants to use cloud software without managing any servers or platforms. Which model is BEST?
explanation: A business that wants software with no servers or platforms to manage should use SaaS.

q: What is the primary benefit of using a cloud provider managed database service?
options: Lower cost than any on-premises option
The provider handles patching, backups, scaling, and availability automatically
explanation: With a managed database service the provider handles patching, backups, scaling, and availability.

q: What software layer allows multiple virtual machines to run simultaneously on a single physical host?
explanation: A hypervisor is the software layer that lets multiple VMs run on one physical host.

q: Which of the following is an example of a Type 2 hypervisor?
explanation: VMware Workstation is a Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor that runs on top of a normal host OS.

q: What is a "sandbox" in the context of virtualization?
options: An isolated VM environment for testing software safely without affecting the host system
explanation: A sandbox is an isolated VM for testing software safely without affecting the host.

q: What BIOS/UEFI setting must be enabled for virtualization software to run virtual machines?
options: Intel VT-x or AMD-V (hardware virtualization support)
explanation: Hardware virtualization (Intel VT-x or AMD-V) must be enabled in BIOS/UEFI to run VMs.

q: What is the main benefit of using VMs for software testing?
options: VMs require less RAM than native installations
VMs always run faster than native installations
Provides isolated environments that can be rolled back or discarded after testing
explanation: VMs give isolated environments that can be rolled back or discarded after testing.

q: What is the minimum consideration when selecting a host PC for running virtual machines?
options: Sufficient RAM, CPU cores, and storage to run both host and guest systems simultaneously
explanation: A VM host needs enough RAM, CPU cores, and storage to run the host plus all guests at once.

q: Which hypervisor technology is built directly into Windows 10 and 11 Pro and later versions?
explanation: Hyper-V is the hypervisor built into Windows 10/11 Pro and later.

q: What resource shortage is MOST likely to cause poor VM performance?
options: USB devices attached to the host
Insufficient RAM allocated to the VM
explanation: Too little RAM allocated to a VM is the most common cause of poor VM performance.

q: What does "guest OS" refer to in virtualization?
options: The operating system on the physical host
The operating system running inside the virtual machine
explanation: The guest OS is the operating system running inside the virtual machine.

q: What does network bridging mode do for a VM?
options: Makes the VM appear as a separate device on the physical network with its own IP address
Gives the VM an isolated private network only
Shares the host IP address via NAT
Prevents the VM from accessing any network
explanation: Bridged networking makes the VM appear as a separate device on the physical network with its own IP.

q: A technician wants to test malware safely. The BEST approach is:
options: Run it directly on the production machine
Test it in an isolated VM with no network access
Run it in a Docker container with network access
Use a separate partition on the same drive
explanation: Test malware in an isolated VM with no network access so it cannot spread.

q: Which virtualization feature passes a physical disk directly to a VM without going through the hypervisor storage layer?
explanation: Disk/device passthrough gives a VM direct access to physical hardware, bypassing the hypervisor storage layer.

q: What is the purpose of VM cloning?
options: Backs up the VM to cloud storage
Creates a snapshot of the current VM state
Migrates the VM to different physical hardware
Creates an identical copy of a VM for rapid deployment or testing
explanation: VM cloning makes an identical copy of a VM for rapid deployment or testing.

q: What does CPU affinity do in VM configuration?
options: Assigns specific physical CPU cores to a VM for dedicated processing
Overclocks the CPU for the VM
explanation: CPU affinity pins specific physical CPU cores to a VM for dedicated processing.

q: Which tool is used to manage VMware virtual machines on a desktop computer?
explanation: VMware Workstation is the tool used to manage VMware virtual machines on a desktop.

q: A PC powers on with fans spinning but no POST and no display output. What component should be reseated FIRST?
explanation: No POST with the fans spinning often means a memory problem; reseating the RAM is the quickest no-cost first step before suspecting the CPU or GPU.

q: A PC emits three short beeps during POST (AMI BIOS) and fails to boot. What does this indicate?
options: RAM error — memory not detected or failed
explanation: On AMI BIOS, three short beeps indicate a RAM/memory error (no memory installed, or memory failure). Note: beep codes are vendor-specific. On AMI BIOS, one short beep = successful POST. Always identify the BIOS manufacturer before diagnosing by beep pattern.

q: What tool measures voltages from a PSU to verify it is providing correct power levels?
explanation: A multimeter or dedicated PSU tester reads the actual voltages on the power connectors to confirm the supply is delivering correct, stable power.

q: A PC randomly freezes and throws BSODs. Running Memtest86 shows errors. What should be replaced?
explanation: Memtest86 tests system memory, so errors there point to faulty RAM — replace the affected module(s).

q: A computer randomly shuts off only under heavy load. Airflow is clear and all fans work. The MOST likely cause is:
options: Inadequate or failing power supply unable to sustain load
explanation: Shutting off only under heavy load, with cooling fine, points to a power supply that cannot sustain the higher current demand.

q: What diagnostic device displays POST codes on a small LED panel and is installed in a PCI or PCIe slot?
explanation: A POST diagnostic card installs in a PCI/PCIe slot and shows hex POST codes that pinpoint where boot-up stalls.

q: A PC displays "CPU fan error" at startup but the fan is visibly spinning. What else could trigger this message?
options: Fan speed below the BIOS minimum threshold, or the fan connected to the wrong header
explanation: A spinning fan can still trip a 'CPU fan error' if its RPM is below the BIOS minimum or it is plugged into the wrong header (e.g., SYS_FAN instead of CPU_FAN).

q: After a BIOS update fails and the system will not POST, what recovery option do some motherboards provide?
options: Dual BIOS or BIOS recovery using a USB flash drive with the correct firmware file
explanation: Many boards offer a BIOS recovery (dual BIOS, or a USB flash recovery) that reflashes known-good firmware when an update fails to POST.

q: What Windows tool tests RAM for errors and can be launched from the Start menu?
explanation: Windows Memory Diagnostic (mdsched.exe) is the built-in RAM tester, launched from the Start menu and run on reboot.

q: What does a BSOD stop code help a technician identify?
options: The specific error type and often the failed driver or component causing the crash
explanation: The stop code identifies the error type and often the specific driver or component that caused the crash, which guides the fix.

q: Which CPU socket type features pins on the motherboard socket and a flat contact pad on the CPU (used by Intel)?
explanation: LGA (Land Grid Array) puts the pins in the motherboard socket and flat contact pads on the CPU — the design Intel uses.

q: A user gets "No bootable device" at startup. The FIRST things to check are:
options: Boot order in BIOS and whether the boot drive is detected
explanation: 'No bootable device' usually means the BIOS boot order is wrong or the boot drive is not being detected — check those first.

q: A hard drive produces a clicking noise during operation. What does this indicate?
options: Drive spinning up normally after a cold start
Mechanical failure — the read/write head is failing, data is at risk — back up immediately
Vibration from a nearby case fan
explanation: A clicking hard drive signals failing read/write heads or mechanics; back up immediately because data loss is imminent.

q: What Windows utility checks and attempts to repair hard drive file system errors and bad sectors?
explanation: chkdsk scans the file system for errors and bad sectors and attempts repairs (chkdsk /f or /r).

q: Which RAID level can survive the simultaneous failure of two drives?
explanation: RAID 6 uses double parity, so it can survive two simultaneous drive failures.

q: A RAID 5 array loses one drive and is now in a degraded state. What should the technician do?
options: Immediately shut down and restore from backup
Replace the failed drive as soon as possible to allow the array to rebuild
Delete the RAID configuration and start over
Continue using it as-is since data is still accessible
explanation: A degraded RAID 5 still runs on parity but has no redundancy left — replace the failed drive promptly so the array can rebuild.

q: What diagnostic feature monitors hard drive health using internal drive statistics such as reallocated sectors?
options: S.M.A.R.T. (Self-Monitoring, Analysis and Reporting Technology) via tools like CrystalDiskInfo
explanation: S.M.A.R.T. reports internal drive health stats like reallocated sectors; tools such as CrystalDiskInfo read them.

q: A newly installed NVMe SSD is not detected in BIOS. What should be checked?
options: Physical seating in the M.2 slot, BIOS M.2 slot enablement, and correct slot type for NVMe vs SATA
explanation: An undetected NVMe SSD is usually a seating issue, a disabled M.2 slot in BIOS, or a slot that is SATA-only rather than NVMe.

q: A user wants to clone their current HDD to a new SSD. What type of tool is used?
options: Disk cloning software such as Clonezilla or Macrium Reflect
explanation: Disk-cloning tools like Macrium Reflect or Clonezilla copy the whole drive, including the OS, onto the new SSD.

q: What does a S.M.A.R.T. status of "Caution" or "Failing" indicate?
options: Drive is operating normally with minor warnings
Drive has detected internal errors and potential imminent failure — back up data immediately
explanation: A 'Caution' or 'Failing' S.M.A.R.T. status means the drive has detected internal errors and may fail soon — back up now.

q: A storage drive appears in BIOS but not in Windows. The MOST likely solution is:
options: Initialize the drive and create a partition using Windows Disk Management
explanation: A drive seen in BIOS but not in Windows typically just needs to be initialized and partitioned in Disk Management.

q: Which RAID type offers the best read and write performance with no redundancy?
explanation: RAID 0 stripes data across drives for the best read/write speed but offers no redundancy — losing one drive loses everything.

q: What is the FIRST action when a critical drive begins showing S.M.A.R.T. warnings?
options: Back up all data immediately before any further action
explanation: When S.M.A.R.T. warns of trouble, backing up data comes before any repair attempt that could stress a dying drive.

q: A monitor displays "No Signal." The PC is powered on and the cable is confirmed secure. What should be checked NEXT?
options: Confirm the correct input source is selected on the monitor
explanation: 'No signal' with power and cable confirmed usually means the monitor is set to the wrong input source.

q: A display shows a flickering image. After replacing the video cable with no improvement, what is the NEXT component to suspect?
options: The monitor panel itself or the GPU
explanation: If a new cable does not fix the flicker, the fault is in the monitor panel itself or the GPU driving it.

q: What is "pixel pitch" in a display specification?
options: The distance between centers of adjacent pixels — smaller pitch means a sharper image
explanation: Pixel pitch is the distance between the centers of adjacent pixels; a smaller pitch packs pixels tighter for a sharper image.

q: A laptop screen is black but an external monitor connected via HDMI works fine. What should be checked?
options: Laptop display cable, backlight, or LCD panel
explanation: A black laptop screen while an external display works points to the laptop's own display cable, backlight, or LCD panel.

q: What does "dead pixel" mean on a display?
options: A pixel stuck on a bright color permanently
A pixel that never illuminates and remains black regardless of the displayed content
A burnt-in image on the screen
A cluster of bright pixels from overheating
explanation: A dead pixel stays black and never lights up regardless of content (a stuck pixel is the opposite — stuck on a color).

q: A user second monitor shows only a portion of the desktop with the image cut off at edges. What resolves this?
options: Overscan or underscan setting adjustment, or correcting the display resolution
explanation: An image cut off at the edges is usually overscan/underscan or a mismatched resolution; adjust those to fit the screen.

q: What is the FIRST thing to check when a projector displays "no signal"?
options: Confirm the correct input source is selected and the cable is connected
explanation: As with monitors, a projector 'no signal' is most often the wrong input source or a loose cable — check that first.

q: A monitor displays in portrait orientation when it should be landscape. What is the fix?
options: Adjust display orientation in Windows display settings
explanation: A sideways image is fixed in Windows display settings by setting the orientation back to landscape.

q: What GPU temperature range is generally considered acceptable under full load for most consumer graphics cards?
options: 70-85 degrees C (above 95 degrees is a concern for most cards)
explanation: Most consumer GPUs run fine around 70-85°C under full load; sustained temps above ~95°C are a concern.

q: A projector image appears trapezoidal rather than rectangular. What adjustment corrects this?
explanation: A trapezoidal projector image is corrected with keystone adjustment, which squares up the picture.

q: What is the MOST common reason an HDMI monitor connected to a laptop shows no signal even with a good cable?
options: Display output mode not configured — use Win+P to select the correct display mode
explanation: Even with a good cable, a laptop often shows no external signal until the display mode is set — press Win+P to choose Duplicate or Extend.

q: What does refresh rate measure in a display?
options: How many times per second the screen redraws the image, in hertz (Hz)
The number of pixels per inch
The physical size of the display
explanation: Refresh rate is how many times per second the display updates its image, in Hz (e.g., 60 or 144 Hz) — higher looks smoother.

q: A GPU shows artifacting on screen with normal temperatures. After testing with a different monitor and same result, what is MOST likely?
options: Driver corruption or failing GPU VRAM
explanation: Artifacting that persists on a second monitor at normal temps points to corrupted drivers or failing GPU VRAM, not the display.

q: A smartphone will not charge. After trying different cables and chargers with no improvement, what should be inspected?
options: The charging port for debris, lint, or physical damage
explanation: When cables and chargers are ruled out, inspect the charging port for lint or physical damage before replacing anything.

q: A mobile device battery drains faster than normal after a software update. The FIRST step is:
options: Check for apps using excessive battery, restart the device, or consider rolling back the update
explanation: After an update, sudden battery drain is usually a misbehaving app or process — check battery usage, restart, or roll back before drastic steps.

q: A tablet touchscreen is unresponsive in one corner. What should be tried FIRST?
options: Restart the device and attempt touchscreen recalibration
explanation: An unresponsive touch area is often cleared by a restart and touchscreen recalibration before any hardware replacement.

q: A smartphone camera produces blurry photos regardless of lighting or distance. The MOST likely cause is:
options: Camera lens is smudged or the optical image stabilization module is faulty
explanation: Blurry photos in all conditions usually mean a smudged lens or a faulty optical image stabilization module.

q: What does a mobile device typically do when it overheats as a protective measure?
options: Performance throttling occurs followed by automatic shutdown if cooling is insufficient
explanation: To protect itself, an overheating device throttles performance and will shut down automatically if it cannot cool.

q: A mobile device has weak Wi-Fi even when close to the router. All other devices connect normally. What should be checked?
options: Device Wi-Fi antenna connection or the device wireless adapter
explanation: Weak Wi-Fi on just one device, close to the router, points to that device's Wi-Fi antenna or wireless adapter.

q: What does a soft reset (restart) of a mobile device accomplish?
options: Clears temporary memory and restarts OS processes without data loss
Erases all user data and apps
explanation: A soft reset clears temporary memory and restarts the OS processes without erasing any user data.

q: A smartphone GPS is inaccurate. After confirming GPS is enabled, what else can improve accuracy?
options: Toggle location services off and on, or ensure A-GPS is enabled with Wi-Fi or cellular data available
Remove and reinsert the SIM card
explanation: Inaccurate GPS often improves by toggling location services and enabling A-GPS, which uses Wi-Fi/cellular to speed and sharpen the fix.

q: What is the purpose of MDM (Mobile Device Management) software?
options: Centrally manage, secure, monitor, and enforce policies across mobile devices in an organization
explanation: Mobile Device Management centrally secures, monitors, and enforces policies across an organization's mobile devices.

q: A mobile device cannot make or receive calls but connects to Wi-Fi normally. The MOST likely cause is:
options: SIM card issue or cellular service problem
explanation: Calling fails but Wi-Fi works, so the cellular side is the problem — typically a SIM or carrier service issue.

q: What does enabling Do Not Disturb mode on a mobile device do?
options: Silences calls, notifications, and alerts based on configured schedule and exceptions
explanation: Do Not Disturb silences calls, notifications, and alerts according to its schedule and allowed exceptions.

q: A mobile app crashes immediately on launch. After clearing the app cache with no improvement, what is the NEXT step?
options: Clear app data or uninstall and reinstall the app
explanation: If clearing the cache does not fix an app crash, clear its data or uninstall and reinstall before resetting the whole device.

q: What is the FIRST step if a mobile device displays "SIM not detected"?
options: Contact the carrier for a replacement SIM
Remove and firmly reseat the SIM card in the tray
explanation: 'SIM not detected' is first addressed by powering off and firmly reseating the SIM in its tray.

q: A laser printer produces pages where the toner smears or rubs off easily. The MOST likely failing component is:
explanation: Toner that smears or rubs off was never fused to the paper — the fuser assembly (heat and pressure) is failing.

q: A printer produces a blank page every time it prints. The FIRST thing to check is:
options: Toner or ink level, and whether protective tape was removed from a new cartridge
explanation: A blank page is usually an empty cartridge or protective tape left on a new one — check that before drivers or cables.

q: What does the Windows print spooler service do?
options: Physically routes cables to the printer
Manages and queues print jobs between applications and the printer
explanation: The print spooler queues and manages print jobs between applications and the printer.

q: A laser printer produces a repeating smudge or mark at regular intervals on every page. The MOST likely cause is:
options: Contamination or damage on the drum or rollers at the interval matching the drum circumference
explanation: Repeating defects at regular intervals are caused by a contaminated or damaged component that repeats on every rotation. The interval distance equals the circumference of the offending part. Drum circumference (~94 mm for a typical cartridge) repeats every ~3.7 inches. If the interval is shorter, su

q: What does "toner scatter" appearing as speckles around text on laser-printed pages typically indicate?
options: Damaged drum, high humidity, or incorrect paper type
explanation: Toner scatter/speckling around text points to a worn drum, high humidity, or the wrong paper type.

q: A network printer worked yesterday but shows offline today with no known changes. The FIRST thing to check is:
options: Verify the printer IP address has not changed due to DHCP lease expiration
explanation: A printer suddenly 'offline' with no changes often got a new IP from DHCP — verify or reserve its address.

q: What causes "ghosting" on a laser-printed page — a faint duplicate image offset from the main image?
options: Worn drum unit that is not fully discharging residual charge after the transfer step
explanation: Drum ghosting: a worn drum retains residual charge from a prior print cycle, attracting toner in that same pattern on subsequent pages, creating a faint ghost of an earlier image. Fuser ghosting is a distinct failure mode: an underheated fuser partially bonds toner, which remelts further down the sa

q: A laser printer produces streaked output. After replacing the toner cartridge with no improvement, what should be checked next?
explanation: Streaks that remain after a new toner cartridge point to the drum unit as the next suspect.

q: A printer prints in draft quality even though the quality setting in the print dialog appears correct. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: Whether the correct printer driver for this exact model is installed
explanation: Output stuck in draft despite correct dialog settings usually means the wrong or generic driver is installed for that exact model.

q: A user can access all local network resources but cannot reach the internet. What is MOST likely misconfigured?
explanation: Local resources reachable but no internet points to a missing or wrong default gateway — the exit to other networks.

q: A user device has an IP address of 169.254.x.x. What does this indicate?
options: DHCP failed and the device self-assigned an APIPA address
A static IP was set incorrectly
explanation: A 169.254.x.x address is APIPA — the device self-assigned it because it could not reach a DHCP server.

q: Which command tests basic network connectivity to a remote host?
explanation: ping sends ICMP echoes to test basic reachability of a remote host.

q: A workstation cannot access any network resources but ipconfig shows a valid IP address. What should be tested NEXT?
explanation: With a valid IP but no access, ping the default gateway next to see whether the problem is local or beyond the router.

q: What does the nslookup command do?
options: Queries DNS servers to resolve hostnames to IP addresses for troubleshooting
explanation: nslookup queries DNS servers to resolve hostnames to IP addresses, isolating name-resolution problems.

q: A user on a wireless network has slow speeds while others nearby have fast speeds. The MOST likely cause is:
options: ISP is throttling that specific device
The user device is on the 2.4 GHz band or is far from the router — try switching to 5 GHz
DNS server issue specific to that device
explanation: One device slow while others are fast often means it is on the congested 2.4 GHz band or far from the router — try 5 GHz.

q: What sequence of commands releases the current DHCP lease and requests a new IP address in Windows?
explanation: ipconfig /release drops the current DHCP lease and ipconfig /renew requests a fresh address from the DHCP server.

q: Which command displays all active network connections and listening ports on a Windows PC?
explanation: netstat lists active connections and listening ports; netstat -ano also shows the process ID that owns each one.

q: What does "channel bonding" do in Wi-Fi networking?
options: Combines two or more adjacent channels to increase bandwidth (e.g., 40 MHz, 80 MHz, or 160 MHz channels)
Combines two frequency bands for enhanced security
Pairs the router with a specific device MAC address
explanation: Channel bonding combines adjacent Wi-Fi channels (40/80/160 MHz) to widen the pipe and raise throughput.

q: A user cannot browse websites but pinging 8.8.8.8 succeeds. What command directly verifies whether DNS is resolving names correctly?
explanation: Pinging 8.8.8.8 works but names do not resolve, so use nslookup to test DNS directly.

q: What is the purpose of the netsh winsock reset command?
options: Resets the Windows network stack (Winsock catalog) to fix corruption issues
Resets the router to factory defaults
explanation: netsh winsock reset rebuilds the Windows network stack (Winsock catalog) to clear corruption causing connectivity issues.

q: A newly installed switch port shows an amber LED instead of green when a device is connected. What does this typically indicate?
options: Link speed of 10 or 100 Mbps instead of gigabit, or a fault condition depending on switch model
explanation: An amber port LED usually means a reduced link speed (10/100 instead of gigabit) or a fault, depending on the switch.
